name: Participatory-web promotional principles
description: The conference and startup vocabulary that presented the participatory web as a distinct technological phase.
cause_of_death: Semantic diffusion, saturation, and documented loss of promotional novelty by 2009; the technologies continued.

sources.title: What Is Web 2.0
sources.note: Primary statement of the promotional framework; not evidence that each slogan was newly coined.

sources.title: Web2.0
sources.note: Contemporary list of named principles and discussion of semantic diffusion.

sources.title: The Death Of "Web 2.0"
sources.note: Contemporary report describes Google Trends growth during 2005 through end-2007 and decline thereafter.

sources.title: What Bruce Sterling Actually Said About Web 2.0 at Webstock 09
sources.note: Speech transcript reports lost novelty and interrogates slogans including architecture of participation and folksonomy.

sources.title: Web 2.0
sources.note: Retrospective reference explicitly lists perpetual beta; exact historical dating relies on contemporary sources elsewhere.

entries.gloss: A promotional designation for the participatory web as a new cultural and commercial phase.

examples.text: Could you give these printouts the Web 2.0 treatment and share them with the team?

entries.rationale: The term is curated as a promotional slogan of the Web 2.0 moment, not as a claim that its underlying practice vanished. Contemporary 2005/2006 statements attest the form; 2009 criticism establishes saturation and lost novelty. Onset and peak interpolate the 2004 conference-to-2007 publicity interval; the 2011 fade is an estimated register boundary, not a measured last use. Context terms restrict retrieval to the attested semantic domain; these lexical hints do not alter historical dating or establish new usage evidence.
